widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is one single adult East Asian woman, about 50 years old, whose facial identity is anchored first by <Picture 1>, whose full-body clothing and proportions are anchored by <Picture 2>, and whose side and rear silhouette are anchored by <Picture 3>. <Picture 1> is a close, straight-on face reference for the same mature oval face, calm dark brown eyes, natural brows, nose, lips, jawline, warm fair skin, and dark-brown hairline gathered into one compact neat high bun. <Picture 2> is the same woman's full-body reference: slim natural dancer proportions, dusty mauve-pink fitted long-sleeve V-neck top with subtle center gathering, matching full-length wide-leg trousers, and cream flat dance shoes. <Picture 3> is the same woman's left side and rear-silhouette reference: nose and chin profile, neck, shoulders, hips, trousers, and compact bun. These three pictures are one woman, never three people.
<Subject 2> is the stable indoor dance studio from <Video 1>: pale wall, large red Chinese lettering, horizontal ballet barres, green floor, ceiling lights, and cool greenish fluorescent lighting.
<Video 1> is the source motion and composition reference. It supplies choreography, body trajectory, pose timing, facial gesture timing, orientation, camera timing, and studio layout only. It does not provide the target identity, face, hairstyle, black shirt, blue jeans, or body appearance.
<Picture 4> is the actual first frame of the target segment. It is a concrete temporal anchor, not an identity reference. The segment must begin with the same dancer pose, body position, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, background, and scene composition shown in <Picture 4>.

<Picture 5> is the actual last frame of the target segment. It is a concrete temporal anchor, not an identity reference. The segment must end with the same dancer pose, body position, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, background, and scene composition shown in <Picture 5>.

<Picture 4> and <Picture 5> use the same canvas, camera geometry, background plate, lighting, and scene layout. They define the temporal endpoints of one continuous segment and must not be treated as additional characters.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation + keyframe completion + audio reuse] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>, re-performed by <Subject 1>. <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, and <Picture 3> define the identity of the same Yumei. <Picture 4> is the actual first frame of this segment and <Picture 5> is the actual last frame. Preserve the choreography, camera movement, studio layout, and original audio from <Video 1>, while continuously transforming the dancer into Yumei from <Picture 4> to <Picture 5>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears throughout the complete target): attribute_transfer - transfer one coherent woman from the three identity pictures onto every segment and pose. The face from <Picture 1> is the highest-priority identity constraint and must not change age, eye shape, nose, lips, jawline, skin tone, or expression style. Keep the compact high bun, mauve-pink outfit, slim proportions, cream shoes, and natural body anatomy stable through front, side, rear, and near-camera views. The identity must not reset at a segment boundary.
<Subject 2> (appears throughout the complete target): fully_preserved - retain the studio wall, red Chinese lettering, ballet barres, green floor, fluorescent lighting, and source camera perspective as stable scene guidance.
<Video 1> (choreography, body trajectory, pose timing, orientation, framing, camera timing, and studio layout): fully_preserved - follow the source movement continuously and beat by beat while replacing the dancer's identity and clothing.
<Picture 4> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the target segment begins from this exact pose, body placement, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, and background composition.
<Picture 5> ([Shot 1] last frame): fully_preserved - the target segment ends on this exact pose, body placement, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, and background composition.
<Picture 4> and <Picture 5> (temporal endpoints): fully_preserved - they are the first and last frames of the same continuous segment, not additional identity references or separate characters.


detailed_description:
The target is a realistic 24 fps single-take dance-studio re-performance. <Subject 1> remains one single adult woman throughout the entire segment.

[Shot 1] The segment begins exactly from <Picture 4>. Preserve its dancer pose, body location, facing direction, gaze, camera framing, background, lighting, and spatial composition as the opening state. The dancer then follows <Video 1> continuously and beat by beat, preserving its choreography, body trajectory, rhythm, footwork, weight transfers, arm paths, hand gestures, orientation, and camera timing. The movement must develop continuously from <Picture 4> without pausing, restarting, resetting, or changing identity. The motion gradually converges toward <Picture 5>, and the segment ends exactly on the pose, body location, facing direction, gaze, framing, lighting, background, and spatial composition shown in <Picture 5>. <Picture 5> is the final temporal endpoint, not an additional identity image.
Hands must look like ordinary anatomically correct human hands attached to the arms. Use small, relaxed, softly curved hands with fingers naturally grouped together; do not create long pointed fingers, ornate ballet claws, finger fans, fused fingers, extra fingers, missing fingers, detached wrists, double wrists, or rubber-like stretching. Do not make the fingers a visual focus. Preserve the source arm direction and palm orientation, but simplify finger detail whenever the hand is distant or moving quickly. Keep the forearm, wrist, palm, and fingers as one coherent structure.
Across the first segment boundary, preserve the last pose and movement direction from the preceding clean delivery. Do not restart the body, change the camera, or change the identity. During turning and rear-view phases, use <Picture 3> to keep the bun, neck, shoulder line, back neckline, hips, and trousers coherent. Keep the entire body in natural balance and avoid sudden limb length changes.
During the return toward camera and the hand-near-face gesture, keep the face exactly in the identity family of <Picture 1>: same age, facial geometry, eye spacing, nose, lips, jawline, skin tone, and compact bun. Do not beautify, rejuvenate, redraw, or morph the face between frames. Keep the nearer forearm in front of the face and the farther arm behind it with stable depth ordering. Across the second segment boundary, continue the same pose, camera direction, studio geometry, lighting, and motion momentum from the previous clean delivery; never snap to a new stance or alter the wall lettering.
For the wider centered stance, knee bend, raised-arm phrase, lateral-arm extension, and final hand-across-neck phrase, preserve the source timing and body trajectory. The Chain Context continuation must extend the preceding clean delivery rather than inventing a new gesture. End on the same final pose, framing, studio, and audio timing as <Video 1>. No visible pose graphics, no skeleton lines, no magenta dots, no extra characters, no dialogue, no subtitles, no new props, no background replacement, and no new music. <Audio 1> remains continuous.

overall_soundscape:
The copied studio room tone and synchronized production sound from <Audio 1> continue throughout the complete performance.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A; no new audience-only music is added.
